page: Amazon Web Services r3.large is a legacy generation memory-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates one physical core hyperthreaded to provide two dedicated vCPUs, backed by 25 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 15.0 GB, delivering 7.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local ephemeral storage includes a bundled 32 GB SSD, while hardware accelerators are absent.

Across performance benchmarks, the r3.large demonstrates legacy-tier output. Geekbench scores reach 700.0 for single-core and 813.0 for multi-core evaluations, placing compute throughput in the bottom tier relative to modern cloud infrastructure. PassMark testing records a CPU score of 1924.04 and a database operations metric of 711.93. Memory throughput measures 13.3 GB/s for large-block read operations and 11.51 GB/s for writes. In-memory data access yields 0.75 million Redis SET operations per second, with static web delivery reaching 1.89 GB/s.

The hardware profile offers a relatively high memory-to-vCPU allocation accompanied by local solid-state storage. However, its older Ivy Bridge architecture lacks contemporary instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and BMI2, which limits computational efficiency per resource slice. While the 15.0 GB memory capacity provides adequate space for moderate memory footprints, the underlying single-core execution speed and 0 Gbps baseline network throttle data ingestion. The instance serves legacy in-memory caching, small relational databases, or lightweight staging environments requiring substantial memory headroom over raw compute throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services r3.large is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by a dual-threaded single physical core from an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor at 2.5 GHz. Configured on the Xen hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, it provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs, 15.0 GB of system memory, and a 32 GB local SSD volume without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks reflect its legacy hardware profile, recording a PassMark CPU score of 1924.04, a Geekbench multi-core score of 813.0, and Redis throughput of 0.75 million SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers 13.3 GB/s for uncached reads alongside 11.51 GB/s writes. Lacking newer instruction sets like AVX-512, computational density is restrained relative to modern alternatives. The r3.large fits legacy workloads needing a high memory-to-vCPU allocation, such as small caching layers, lightweight relational databases, and background staging tasks.
